clue.text: A product of confined sewers in the past?

definitions.text: A product of confined sewers in the past?

parts.words: A product of confined sewers in the past?
parts.note: sewers here are people who sew, not drains; prisoners locked up in British jails were once set to stitch canvas sacks for the Post Office

explanation.definitionFit: Stitching sacks for carrying post was the classic task given to convicts in British prisons.

clue.text: Inspiration sought by detectives?

parts.note: inspiration here is what drives a criminal to act, which investigators look for when solving a crime

explanation.definitionFit: A reason that drives someone to act is what detectives look for behind a crime.

clue.text: Popular honour awarded in course of Korean port battle

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British award
on means in progress, as in a match that is on

explanation.surface: A well-liked soldier is decorated during a battle at a port in Korea.
explanation.definitionFit: Inchon is a port in South Korea where a famous 1950 amphibious landing battle took place.

clue.text: Painter's bill to cite restoration

indicators.note: restoration suggests rebuilding something, so these letters are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: An artist's invoice quotes the cost of restoring a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Botticelli was the Florentine Renaissance artist who painted The Birth of Venus.

clue.text: Gin that is a mixture of bottled spirits

indicators.note: a mixture of means the letters are blended together in a new order

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for that is (id est)

explanation.surface: A gin cocktail blends various spirits from bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottled spirits' looks like liquor; it means the genies kept in lamps or bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: Jinn or genies of Arabian tales are spirits that are often trapped inside bottles or lamps.

clue.text: Erudite composer shown the way out

indicators.note: the word for shown the way is opened out so that the composer can sit within it

parts.note: to be shown the way is to be led
Thomas Arne, the English composer of Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: A scholarly musician is escorted to the exit.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'shown the way out' sound like being ejected; 'out' instead tells you to open up one word round another. Thomas Arne is a crossword favourite among composers.
explanation.definitionFit: An erudite person has deep book knowledge, which is what a scholarly, well-read person is.

clue.text: Wildcat strikes may put one out of work

definitions.text: Wildcat strikes may put one out of work

parts.words: Wildcat strikes may put one out of work
parts.note: a wildcat strike is usually an unofficial walkout, but here it is a wild big cat literally striking at the circus performer who trains it

explanation.definitionFit: A circus performer who trains big cats could be injured by a lion lashing out with a paw.

clue.text: Point primate out in church

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order and rearranged

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: Someone points out a monkey loose in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the rounded recess at the east end of a church, so it is found in church.

clue.text: A last drink for the head on retirement

definitions.meaning: a final drink taken before bed
a soft hat worn in bed, retirement meaning going to bed

explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a last drink before sleep and a cap once worn in bed.

clue.text: Little Sidney turned the lock, causing much trouble

indicators.note: turned means the short name is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: Sid is the short form of Sidney
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A small boy turns a key in a lock and causes great trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses SID to DIS; 'the lock' is hair, not a door lock.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress is great suffering or anxiety, so much trouble is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Bound by discretion, one is silent

indicators.note: one is tied up within the word for discretion, so it is placed inside it

parts.note: discretion or diplomacy is tact
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Someone sworn to discretion stays quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means unspoken or understood without words, so silent is a near synonym.

clue.text: They may advertise in glowing terms

definitions.text: They may advertise in glowing terms

parts.words: They may advertise in glowing terms
parts.note: in glowing terms usually means with lavish praise, but here it means literally in lit-up words, such as illuminated gas tubes over shops

explanation.definitionFit: Illuminated tube signs over shops and bars advertise their wares in letters that literally glow.

clue.text: They bow during and after their performances

definitions.text: They bow during and after their performances

parts.words: They bow during and after their performances
parts.note: bowing after a show is taking applause, but during it these players draw a bow across strings

explanation.definitionFit: String players use a bow while they play, then bow to the audience when they finish.

clue.text: Starts to serve time in Russian prison

indicators.note: the opening letters of the next four words are taken, as their starts

explanation.surface: Someone begins a sentence in a Russian jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is British slang for jail, as in doing time in stir.

clue.text: Don boasted about discovering famous journalist's final words?

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: An academic brags about uncovering a celebrated writer's last words.
explanation.walkthrough: The journalist is the diarist Samuel Pepys, who often ended his daily entries with this phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Pepys habitually closed his diary entries with this phrase, his final words each day.

clue.text: They recommend its men to sail abroad

indicators.note: abroad suggests going all over the place, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: References praise the crew who will go sailing overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Written references and commendations are statements that recommend someone, so they recommend.

clue.text: Firm can set out to restrict debt

indicators.note: to restrict means to hold in, so one piece encloses the other
set out suggests laying things out differently, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an IOU is a written acknowledgement of a debt

explanation.surface: A company sets out to limit its borrowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns the letters of 'can set' into TENACS, and 'to restrict' means that word holds the debt inside it, just ahead of its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenacious means holding fast, so a firm grip or firm resolve is tenacious.

clue.text: Struggles to break a lock, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a lock is a wrestling hold, which a grappler tries to break out of

explanation.definitionFit: To grapple is to struggle, and grapplers fight to break holds such as headlocks.

clue.text: The strength of the current?

parts.note: the current sounds like a flow of water, but here it is electric current measured in amps

explanation.definitionFit: The size of an electric current is measured in amps, so its strength is its measure in amps.

clue.text: Seen in the garden, perhaps incoherent with wine

parts.note: rambling speech wanders and is incoherent
rosé is a pink wine

explanation.surface: A drunk babbling in the garden after too much wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing variety of rose grown over walls and arches is a familiar garden plant.

clue.text: Umpire crooked and corrupt

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A bent referee is dishonest and corrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: Impure means tainted or debased, so corrupt is a fitting synonym.

clue.text: Revised diet arranged with Edward

indicators.note: arranged signals that the letters of the word are set in a new order

parts.note: Ed is the short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A revised eating plan is drawn up with a man called Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: A text that has been edited has been revised and corrected.

clue.text: Duck! It's Captain Hook's bosun!

definitions.meaning: an old dialect name for a duck, such as the wigeon or smew
in Peter Pan, the pirate captain's boatswain is Mr ...

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a dialect bird name for a duck and the pirate in Peter Pan.

clue.text: Familiar routine

definitions.meaning: familiar with something, as in used to it
habitual or usual, as in one's usual habits

explanation.definitionFit: Being used to something makes it familiar, and a habitual practice is a routine one.

clue.text: Unqualified to make a statement

definitions.meaning: complete or absolute, as in total nonsense

explanation.definitionFit: Absolute or complete is one sense, and to speak or say words aloud is the other.

clue.text: Yank involved in weightlifting

definitions.meaning: the clean and ... is an Olympic weightlifting lift

explanation.definitionFit: A sharp tug is a yank, and the second part of a two-stage Olympic lift shares the word.

clue.text: Deals exclusively with signs of spring

definitions.meaning: omits or excludes, a verb phrase
new foliage appearing on trees, a noun phrase with an adverb

explanation.definitionFit: To omit is to exclude, and buds opening on trees show foliage emerging in spring.

clue.text: Straight to the point? But there is no point!

definitions.meaning: lacking a sharp tip or edge

explanation.definitionFit: Plain-spoken frankness and a dull, unsharpened edge are both described by this one adjective.

clue.text: Arab leaders trembling in speech

indicators.note: in speech signals that the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: trembling means shakes, as a noun for the shivers

explanation.surface: Middle Eastern rulers shiver while giving a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheikhs are chiefs of Arab tribes, families or states, so they are leaders.

clue.text: Communist leader is a flaming capitalist

parts.note: a red is a Communist
a head is a leader or chief

explanation.surface: A Communist chief turns out to be a fervent capitalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flaming capitalist' reads as a passionate tycoon, but means someone whose capital, or head, is fiery.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with ginger hair has a top, or capital, that looks as if it were on fire.
